about: Findings of test_logos.ties()'s closer-dot rule (#379: another dot within 9 px of a logo box, or closer to it than the logo's own dot) on maps Erik approved, which the operator chose to keep as delivered rather than move (reddoor-workspace decisions/2026-11-17-1939-roalson-closer-dot-check-fails-approved-maps.md, answer (a)). Per listing and business as the map prints it: `box` is the logo's box [l, t, r, b], and `dots` is every dot near the logo box (test_logos.near_dots()) by kind, business name, distance from the box and centre (`at`), in CSS px: the map must still have exactly those, each within 0.5 px of its distance and its centre, so a logo or a dot that moves, or a dot that goes or appears, fails. Only closer-dot findings are taken off. Read by build/test_logos.py approved(), which build/logo_check.py and test_logos.py's renders use.

Walmart Supercenter.why: Costco's dot sits 6.6 px under the Walmart logo, whose own dot is 8.0 px away (#379). Erik approved the option C maps on 11-17: "The rest look good to me."

Costco.why: Ross's dot is 5.3 px from the Costco logo, which hangs on a line from its own dot (#379). Erik approved the option C maps on 11-17: "The rest look good to me."

Walmart Supercenter.why: The 7,948 count's dot is 7.7 px from the Walmart logo, as near as Walmart's own dot (#379). Erik approved the option C maps on 11-17: "The rest look good to me."

The Home Depot.why: Whataburger's dot is 8.8 px from The Home Depot logo, whose own dot is 8.0 px away (found 2026-11-17, not in #379). Erik approved this map with his 11-17 asks (Whataburger added there): "The rest look good to me."
